findings.title: CI reads the record stage instead of the projected stage
findings.diagnosis: CI uses the last record Stage. Approved transition records store the source stage. Resolution records can omit Stage. CI can reject a permitted current stage or evaluate a stage the run has left.
findings.expected: CI must evaluate the committed current stage and select a corresponding applicable approval.
findings.actual: CI uses the last record Stage. Approved transition records store the source stage. Resolution records can omit Stage. CI can reject a permitted current stage or evaluate a stage the run has left.

evidence.observation: CI uses the last record Stage. Approved transition records store the source stage. Resolution records can omit Stage. CI can reject a permitted current stage or evaluate a stage the run has left.

fix.action: Use ProjectStageState for CI legality and evidence-record stage. Select the bound approval by the intended CI check, rather than the latest arbitrary Approval pointer.
fix.why: CI must evaluate the committed current stage and select a corresponding applicable approval.

verification.method: Run CI after IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZATION -> IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW and after an appended resolution. Also test VERIFICATION -> INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION. Assert projected-stage behavior and no fallback to an unrelated approval.
verification.expected: Meet the expected behavior. Reject the negative controls without changing stored bytes.

fix.tradeoffs: A projected stage alone does not supply a produced-head approval where the preceding source-stage approval never bound one.
fix.alternative: Require an explicit validated CI request bound to the projected stage. This changes more CLI surface.

findings.closure_criterion: Run CI after IMPLEMENTATION_AUTHORIZATION -> IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW and after an appended resolution. Also test VERIFICATION -> INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION. Assert projected-stage behavior and no fallback to an unrelated approval.

findings.title: Host append has no interrupted-write recovery
findings.diagnosis: Append writes a numbered record before the head. The crash-window byte state (durable record, missing head) fails Load with HOST_HEAD_MISMATCH. The independent probe reconstructed that state; it did not kill a process. There is no pending transaction or per-run lock. O_EXCL does prevent two writers from overwriting the same numbered file; lost writes from concurrency were not demonstrated.
findings.expected: Interrupted appends must recover or roll back deterministically without losing a committed record. Concurrent writes must preserve one valid chain.
findings.actual: Append writes a numbered record before the head. The crash-window byte state (durable record, missing head) fails Load with HOST_HEAD_MISMATCH. The independent probe reconstructed that state; it did not kill a process. There is no pending transaction or per-run lock. O_EXCL does prevent two writers from overwriting the same numbered file; lost writes from concurrency were not demonstrated.

evidence.observation: Append writes a numbered record before the head. The crash-window byte state (durable record, missing head) fails Load with HOST_HEAD_MISMATCH. The independent probe reconstructed that state; it did not kill a process. There is no pending transaction or per-run lock. O_EXCL does prevent two writers from overwriting the same numbered file; lost writes from concurrency were not demonstrated.

fix.action: Use a per-run transaction lock and durable pending commit protocol comparable to the core store. Recover before Load/Append and synchronize directory changes where required.
fix.why: Interrupted appends must recover or roll back deterministically without losing a committed record. Concurrent writes must preserve one valid chain.

verification.method: Inject failure after creation, partial record write, fsync, pending intent and head replacement. Restart and assert one valid committed prefix. Exercise separate-process writers and verify every accepted append remains in the chain.
verification.expected: Meet the expected behavior. Reject the negative controls without changing stored bytes.

fix.tradeoffs: Recovery needs an explicit commit point. Blindly trusting the final numbered record could accept an incomplete write.
fix.alternative: Store host events through a shared proven transaction primitive while preserving separate host record semantics.

findings.closure_criterion: Inject failure after creation, partial record write, fsync, pending intent and head replacement. Restart and assert one valid committed prefix. Exercise separate-process writers and verify every accepted append remains in the chain.

findings.expected: A terminal run must refuse new execution-authorizing host operations. Reading historical telemetry can remain allowed.

fix.action: Project core stage/outcome before all host execution mutations. Reject terminal execution and bind the check and append to a consistent core snapshot. Define any allowed post-terminal reporting operation explicitly.
fix.why: A terminal run must refuse new execution-authorizing host operations. Reading historical telemetry can remain allowed.

verification.method: After each supported terminal outcome, refuse decision, preflight and dispatch without byte changes. Test any permitted read/report path separately.

findings.closure_criterion: After each supported terminal outcome, refuse decision, preflight and dispatch without byte changes. Test any permitted read/report path separately.

findings.title: Completed verify-loop import does not integrate its execution authority
findings.diagnosis: The actual controller owns attempts, deadlines, recovery and worker launch through agent-dispatch. It can select an escalation route after failed interventions. The proposed mapping only imports a completed result. It defines no before-each-attempt HMA eligibility, exact-route preflight, dispatch receipt, authority/stop check, or approved escalation bridge. Host counting of dispatch records will miss these inner attempts unless that bridge exists. The current skill also runs workers/checks in a private clone and copies changed paths back; the packet does not bind clone evidence to the returned HMA artifact.

The proposed mapping only imports a completed result. It defines no before-each-attempt HMA eligibility, exact-route preflight, dispatch receipt, authority/stop check, or approved escalation bridge. Host counting of dispatch records will miss these inner attempts unless that bridge exists. The current skill also runs workers/checks in a private clone and copies changed paths back; the packet does not bind clone evidence to the returned HMA artifact.

The proposed mapping only imports a completed result. It defines no before-each-attempt HMA eligibility, exact-route preflight, dispatch receipt, authority/stop check, or approved escalation bridge. Host counting of dispatch records will miss these inner attempts unless that bridge exists. The current skill also runs workers/checks in a private clone and copies changed paths back; the packet does not bind clone evidence to the returned HMA artifact.

fix.action: Choose and document one integration seam before Gate C. findings.title: Audit import can lose findings and lacks acceptance/disposition rules
findings.diagnosis: The audit report uses severity and verdict, while HMA findings use BLOCK/WAIVABLE/ADVISORY. The mapping supplies no deterministic disposition/reference policy or verified per-criterion acceptance. It says each finding becomes a core finding record; current projection replaces the whole nonempty Findings snapshot, so naive one-finding-per-record imports hide earlier findings. Closure at a newer head is an extra condition even when fresh evidence at the same head resolves a non-code gap. A report digest and phase1_frozen field do not establish reviewer independence.

findings.title: Budget comparison is reversed and attempt authority is incomplete
findings.diagnosis: The packet says lease budgets >= envelope budgets are refused, then says the envelope must fit inside the lease. The inequality is reversed. Counting host dispatch rows does not define direct-cost work, inner loop attempts, review dispatches, retries/reroutes, crash reservations or repeated-failure stopping. Token ceilings have no enforcement mechanism. The proposal omits the §17 classification and same-material-failure-twice stop rule.
findings.expected: Reject an envelope that exceeds any remaining lease ceiling. Count all implementation attempts across corrections/reroutes. Do not count a reviewer launch as a new implementation attempt. Fail closed when a claimed hard ceiling is unmeasurable.

limitations: Fresh auditor context. No implementer conversation, prior model reasoning or defense was supplied. The approved plan, baseline packet and reference audit are inherently author-written objects and were read as claims, after independent requirements reconstruction.

Isolation is isolated at the context level. Repository access was read-only by audit procedure, not an OS-enforced read-only mount. The worktree is shared and dirty. No HMA file or Git state was edited by this auditor. Start/end status, diff and per-file manifests are retained.

External AgentSystem verify-loop files changed during inspection: the later skill adds private-clone execution and the script gained matching code. No actual worker dispatch, route hi, real human challenge ceremony, release CI, token/billing metering, external effects or final verified-success flow was exercised. Jev was not exposed through the host tool inventory. The auditor used the orchestrator/auditor decision path and did not substitute another model under the Jev identity.
